editorial:
Imagine spending a slow, sunny summer in the early 90s where the biggest drama is who is visiting your house. You follow 11-year-old Lacy, a kid with a huge imagination who is totally obsessed with her mom, Janet. They have this special, tight bond that feels warm and cozy at first. The vibe is very relaxed, almost like you are just hanging out in a quiet house in Massachusetts, watching life happen in real time. It feels less like a scripted story and more like a memory of being a child and thinking your parents are the center of the universe.

What really makes this work is how natural the acting feels. The conversations aren't polished; they have those awkward pauses and weird turns that real people actually have. It is a slow burn, so if you need explosions or big twists, you might get bored. But if you like character studies, you will love it. You should definitely try to rent it on Apple TV or grab the 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to see all the beautiful, soft colors of the summer scenery. It is a great pick for a quiet Sunday afternoon.
endingExplained: The movie ends with Lacy realizing that her mother is not just a perfect parent, but a person with her own flaws and needs. After the summer visitors leave, the bubble of her childhood innocence pops. You see Lacy grow up a little bit as she understands that her mother's attention is not infinite. The final scenes leave you feeling a bit sad but hopeful, as Lacy starts to find her own identity apart from Janet.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves slow stories about family and growing up.
